evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Marrying two sisters [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); List of forbidden close-kin unions ('uncovering nakedness') [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); A man may not marry his wife's sister as a rival while the wife lives (weight 7.7); A man must not take his father's wife (uncover his father's skirt) (weight 7.1); List of forbidden close-kin unions ('uncovering nakedness') (weight 6.8). Pair score 37.1.

Only in Forbidden sexual unions; the land vomits out its inhabitants: Sexual relations of a man or a woman with an animal are forbidden; Do not follow the practices of Egypt where you lived or of Canaan where you are going; The land, defiled by abominations, vomits out its inhabitants; The person who does God's statutes shall live by them; Lying with a male as with a woman is forbidden; Whether a man may marry his son's (or adopted son's) wife [divergence between the texts]; Marrying or lying with a brother's wife is forbidden; Zihar: a husband declaring his wife 'like my mother's back'; she is not his mother, the saying is false and abhorrent; Giving one's offspring to Molech is forbidden and punished; Intercourse with a menstruating woman is forbidden; Sexual relations with a neighbor's wife are forbidden.

Only in Inheriting women, the dowry, and the forbidden degrees: A husband exchanging one wife for another may not take back anything he gave, even a qinṭār; God wishes to lighten your burden, for the human was created weak; It is forbidden to inherit women against their will or to hold them back to recover gifts; One who cannot afford a free wife may marry a believing slave woman with her people's leave; Foster mothers and foster sisters by nursing are forbidden in marriage; A married slave woman who commits indecency receives half the punishment of a free woman; Man who lies with a slave woman designated to another man: inquiry and guilt offering, not death, because she is not free; The husband gives the bride her marriage gift (ṣaduqa, ajr) as her own; she may freely remit part; Married women are forbidden except those one's right hand possesses (captives); A man marries a slave woman by leave of her owner and with a payment; What becomes of a dead man's widow within his family [contrast between the texts]; Whether a man may take his wife's sister [neutral] [divergence between the texts]; and 2 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

leads.title: Fast of the twenty-fourth and the Levites' historical confession ↔ The indictment of Israel; the Messiah not crucified but raised
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 2 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Israel killed the prophets who warned them (weight 6.1); People make a molten calf while the leader is on the mountain (weight 5.8). Pair score 11.9.

Only in Fast of the twenty-fourth and the Levites' historical confession: God found Abraham's heart faithful (ne'eman) before him; God chose Abram, brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans and renamed him Abraham; Call to bless God 'from everlasting to everlasting'; God's ordinances are those 'which a man shall do and live by them'; 'You give life to them all' - God sustains all creation; God gave his good spirit to instruct the people in the wilderness; Levites stand on a platform and cry out to God with a loud voice; A quarter of the day spent reading the Torah and a quarter confessing and bowing; God made known his holy Sabbath at Sinai; The seed of Israel separate themselves from all foreigners; Drowned enemies sink like a stone or like lead in mighty waters; Closing doxology: glory to your Lord, Lord of might, above what they describe; peace on the messengers; praise to God, Lord of the worlds; and 16 more.

Only in The indictment of Israel; the Messiah not crucified but raised: Every one of the People of the Book will believe in him before his (or their) death; They did not kill the Messiah Jesus nor crucify him; Israel demands 'show us God openly' and is seized by the thunderbolt; Jesus will be a witness against the People of the Book on resurrection day; It was only made to appear so to them (shubbiha lahum); The Jews' grave slander (buhtān) against Mary; Opponents demand a written book brought down from heaven; God gave the rebellious generation 'statutes that were not good and ordinances by which they could not live', defiling them through offering their firstborn; God raised Jesus up to himself; God raises the mountain (al-Tur) over Israel while taking their covenant [divergence between the texts]; Do not charge interest to the poor of my people [response between the texts]; A request to see God, by the prophet or by the people [divergence between the texts]; and 10 more.

Only in Rebellion after the spies' report and the forty-year sentence: Those who slandered the land die by plague; People have tested God 'ten times'; Intercessor argues the nations would say God was unable; Forty years of wandering, a year for each day of scouting [divergence between the texts]; God threatens to destroy a people and put another in its place [divergence between the texts]; Two faithful spies dissent from the majority [divergence between the texts]; People attack without God's ark or leader and are routed; After the people's rebellion the prophet intercedes for them or asks to be separated from them [divergence between the texts]; People propose appointing a leader to go back to Egypt; Caleb has 'another spirit' and follows God fully; God offers to destroy the people and make a nation of the hero instead; The townsfolk say 'we augur ill of you' and threaten to stone the messengers; they reply 'your omen is with you'; and 10 more.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: Without water, purify with clean earth (tayammum), wiping face and hands (weight 7.3). Pair score 7.3.

Only in The red heifer and corpse impurity: Ash mixed with running ('living') water sprinkled to cleanse; Those who prepare the purifying agent are themselves rendered impure; A corpse defiles everyone and every open vessel in the tent; What contact with a corpse does [contrast between the texts]; Description of the cow required by God [divergence between the texts]; Purification by sprinkling on the third and seventh days; Cedar wood, hyssop and scarlet thread used in a purification rite; Contact with a human corpse makes one ritually impure; Unblemished red cow never yoked is burned whole for purifying ash; Blood or water sprinkled seven times; The offender 'shall be cut off from his people' (karet).

Only in Prayer not while drunk; bathing and dry ablution: Do not approach prayer while intoxicated, until you know what you say; One in major impurity (junub) must bathe before prayer, except a traveller passing through; Purification after seminal emission or intercourse [divergence between the texts]; Emission of semen makes a man (and his partner) unclean until evening; No wine before approaching God [divergence between the texts]; One who has had intercourse must wash before approaching the deity's service or prayer; Priests may not drink wine or strong drink when entering the tent.

leads.title: Daughters of Zelophehad; Moses views the land; Joshua commissioned ↔ The fixed shares of inheritance
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 2 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Rules for who inherits and in what order or share [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.7); Whether and how daughters inherit [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.3); Statutory order of inheritance: son, daughter, brothers, father's brothers, nearest kin (weight 7.3); Daughters petition and win the right to inherit when there is no son (weight 6.8). Pair score 29.3.

Only in Daughters of Zelophehad; Moses views the land; Joshua commissioned: Petition so that a dead man's name not be lost from his clan; Leader ordains his successor by laying hands and sharing his 'splendor' (hod); Decisions sought through the priest's Urim; God addressed as 'God of the spirits of all flesh'; Statutory order of inheritance: son, daughter, brothers, father's brothers, nearest kin [divergence between the texts]; Blood relatives are nearer to one another (in inheritance) in God's book; Leader defers an unprecedented legal case to a divine oracle; Leader shown the whole land from a mountaintop but may not enter; Prayer that the people not be 'like sheep without a shepherd'; The great leader is denied entry into the promised land for a lapse.

Only in The fixed shares of inheritance: Shares are distributed only after a bequest (waṣiyya) and debts are paid; Inheritance fixed in fractions (one half, a third, a quarter, a sixth, an eighth, two-thirds); Husband and wife inherit fixed shares from each other; What a daughter inherits when her father leaves no son [divergence between the texts]; Three named daughters (Jemimah, Keziah, Keren-happuch), the most beautiful in the land, inherit among their brothers; Who receives a double share of inheritance [divergence between the texts]; Who fixes the shares of a man's children in his estate [contrast between the texts]; One who dies without parent or child (kalāla): brothers and sisters inherit fixed shares; A son (or brother) inherits the share of two daughters (or sisters); 'These are the bounds (hudud) of God; do not approach (or transgress) them'; Paradise as gardens (of ʿAdn) beneath which rivers flow, where the righteous abide forever.

matches.label: Rules for who inherits and in what order or share
matches.note: Num 27:8-11 ʾîš kî yāmût û-bēn ʾên lô wĕ-haʿăbartem ʾet naḥălātô lĕ-bittô wĕ-ʾim ʾên lô bat ... lĕ-ʾeḥāyw ... la-ʾăḥê ʾābîw ... li-šʾērô ha-qqārōb: a chain of single heirs: son, else daughter, else brothers, father's brothers, nearest kin; Q 4:11-12 li-dh-dhakari mithlu ḥaẓẓi l-unthayayn ... wa-li-abawayhi li-kulli wāḥidin minhumā s-sudusu ... wa-lakum niṣfu mā taraka azwājukum: fixed fractional shares for several heirs at once, daughters with sons, parents, and spouses (absent from Num 27), siblings only for the kalāla. A sequence of exclusive heirs becomes a set of simultaneous shares. The Quran begins yūṣīkumu llāhu 'God charges you' (cf. ḥuqqat mišpāṭ, 27:11).

passages.text: וְאֶל בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל תְּדַבֵּ֣ר לֵאמֹ֑ר אִ֣ישׁ כִּֽי יָמ֗וּת וּבֵן֙ אֵ֣ין ל֔וֹ וְהַֽעֲבַרְתֶּ֥ם אֶת נַחֲלָת֖וֹ לְבִתּֽוֹ
וְאִם אֵ֥ין ל֖וֹ בַּ֑ת וּנְתַתֶּ֥ם אֶת נַחֲלָת֖וֹ לְאֶחָיו
וְאִם אֵ֥ין ל֖וֹ אַחִ֑ים וּנְתַתֶּ֥ם אֶת נַחֲלָת֖וֹ לַאֲחֵ֥י אָבִֽיו

وَلَكُمْ نِصْفُ مَا تَرَكَ أَزْوَٰجُكُمْ إِن لَّمْ يَكُن لَّهُنَّ وَلَدٌ فَإِن كَانَ لَهُنَّ وَلَدٌ فَلَكُمُ ٱلرُّبُعُ مِمَّا تَرَكْنَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ يُوصِينَ بِهَآ أَوْ دَيْنٍ وَلَهُنَّ ٱلرُّبُعُ مِمَّا تَرَكْتُمْ إِن لَّمْ يَكُن لَّكُمْ وَلَدٌ فَإِن كَانَ لَكُمْ وَلَدٌ فَلَهُنَّ ٱلثُّمُنُ مِمَّا تَرَكْتُم مِّنۢ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ تُوصُونَ بِهَآ أَوْ دَيْنٍ وَإِن كَانَ رَجُلٌ يُورَثُ كَلَٰلَةً أَوِ ٱمْرَأَةٌ وَلَهُۥٓ أَخٌ أَوْ أُخْتٌ فَلِكُلِّ وَٰحِدٍ مِّنْهُمَا ٱلسُّدُسُ فَإِن كَانُوٓا۟ أَكْثَرَ مِن ذَٰلِكَ فَهُمْ شُرَكَآءُ فِى ٱلثُّلُثِ مِنۢ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ يُوصَىٰ بِهَآ أَوْ دَيْنٍ غَيْرَ مُضَآرٍّ وَصِيَّةً مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَلِيمٌ

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).

Only in Daughters of Zelophehad; Moses views the land; Joshua commissioned: Petition so that a dead man's name not be lost from his clan; Leader ordains his successor by laying hands and sharing his 'splendor' (hod); Decisions sought through the priest's Urim; God addressed as 'God of the spirits of all flesh'; Rules for who inherits and in what order or share [divergence between the texts]; Whether and how daughters inherit [divergence between the texts]; Blood relatives are nearer to one another (in inheritance) in God's book; Statutory order of inheritance: son, daughter, brothers, father's brothers, nearest kin; Leader shown the whole land from a mountaintop but may not enter; Daughters petition and win the right to inherit when there is no son; Prayer that the people not be 'like sheep without a shepherd'; The great leader is denied entry into the promised land for a lapse.

Only in The final ruling on kalāla: Who inherits the estate of a man who dies without a son [divergence between the texts]; One who dies without parent or child (kalāla): brothers and sisters inherit fixed shares; A son (or brother) inherits the share of two daughters (or sisters); Form: 'They ask you for a ruling (yastaftūnaka); say: God gives you a ruling'.

Q: in imruʾun halaka laysa lahu waladun wa-lahu ukhtun fa-lahā niṣfu mā taraka: a sister takes half, two sisters two thirds, and mixed siblings share li-l-dhakari mithlu ḥaẓẓi l-unthayayn. Q gives fixed fractions; Num gives only an order of heirs.

leads.title: Levitical cities, cities of refuge and the law of homicide ↔ Accidental and deliberate killing of a believer
leads.summary: 3 correspondences read side by side: 1 deliberately changed, 1 opposite ruling, 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Murder distinguished from manslaughter by weapon (iron, stone, wood), enmity and intent (weight 7.7); A place of refuge for one who kills unintentionally [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.1); Whether payment may substitute for a life [contrast between the texts] (weight 6.8). Pair score 21.6.

Only in Levitical cities, cities of refuge and the law of homicide: Manslayer may leave refuge only at the death of the high priest; Shed blood pollutes the land and only the killer's blood atones for it; Forty-eight cities with pasture-lands of measured cubits assigned to the Levites; No ransom (kofer) may be taken for a murderer's life; How many witnesses a charge requires [divergence between the texts]; Same law for the resident alien and the native; Six cities of refuge for the unintentional killer, three on each side of the Jordan; No one put to death on the testimony of a single witness; The 'redeemer of blood' (go'el ha-dam) kills the murderer.

Only in Accidental and deliberate killing of a believer: Deliberate killing of a believer is punished by hell forever, God's wrath and curse; Do not tell one who greets you with peace 'you are not a believer' to seize booty; Whoever cannot pay the expiation fasts two consecutive months; Accidental killing of a believer: free a believing slave and pay blood money (diya) to the family unless they remit it; A place of refuge for one who kills unintentionally; Blood compensation paid to the kin of a man killed who belongs to a people bound by treaty; The penalty for deliberate murder [divergence between the texts]; Whether payment may substitute for a life.

leads.title: Levitical cities, cities of refuge and the law of homicide ↔ Indecency, four witnesses, and the limits of repentance
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: No one put to death on the testimony of a single witness (weight 6.5). Pair score 6.5.

Only in Levitical cities, cities of refuge and the law of homicide: Murder distinguished from manslaughter by weapon (iron, stone, wood), enmity and intent; Manslayer may leave refuge only at the death of the high priest; Shed blood pollutes the land and only the killer's blood atones for it; Forty-eight cities with pasture-lands of measured cubits assigned to the Levites; No ransom (kofer) may be taken for a murderer's life; How many witnesses a charge requires [divergence between the texts]; A place of refuge for one who kills unintentionally [divergence between the texts]; Same law for the resident alien and the native; Whether payment may substitute for a life [contrast between the texts]; Six cities of refuge for the unintentional killer, three on each side of the Jordan; The 'redeemer of blood' (go'el ha-dam) kills the murderer.

Only in Indecency, four witnesses, and the limits of repentance: Women guilty of indecency are confined to houses until death or until God makes a way; Repentance is not accepted from one who repents only when death comes; Four witnesses are required to establish sexual indecency (fāḥisha); Offenders who repent and reform are to be left alone; Penalty for adultery or sexual indecency [contrast between the texts]; How sin committed in ignorance is forgiven [divergence between the texts]; God accepts repentance from those who do evil in ignorance and soon repent; Whether repentance has a time limit [divergence between the texts]; How many witnesses are required [divergence between the texts].

leads.title: Marriage of heiresses within the tribe; colophon of Numbers ↔ The fixed shares of inheritance
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 deliberately changed.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Whether and how daughters inherit [divergence between the texts] (weight 7.3); Daughters petition and win the right to inherit when there is no son (weight 6.8). Pair score 14.2.

Only in Marriage of heiresses within the tribe; colophon of Numbers: The Jubilee year considered in tribal land transfers; Daughters who inherit must marry within their father's tribe so land does not pass away; The marriage of fatherless girls is tied to their inheritance [divergence between the texts].

Only in The fixed shares of inheritance: Shares are distributed only after a bequest (waṣiyya) and debts are paid; Inheritance fixed in fractions (one half, a third, a quarter, a sixth, an eighth, two-thirds); Husband and wife inherit fixed shares from each other; What a daughter inherits when her father leaves no son [divergence between the texts]; Three named daughters (Jemimah, Keziah, Keren-happuch), the most beautiful in the land, inherit among their brothers; Who receives a double share of inheritance [divergence between the texts]; Who fixes the shares of a man's children in his estate [contrast between the texts]; One who dies without parent or child (kalāla): brothers and sisters inherit fixed shares; A son (or brother) inherits the share of two daughters (or sisters); Rules for who inherits and in what order or share [divergence between the texts]; 'These are the bounds (hudud) of God; do not approach (or transgress) them'; Statutory order of inheritance: son, daughter, brothers, father's brothers, nearest kin; and 1 more.

matches.label: Whether and how daughters inherit
matches.note: Num 36:8 wĕ-kol bat yōrešet naḥălâ ... lĕ-ʾeḥād mi-mmišpaḥat maṭṭēh ʾābîhā tihyeh lĕ-ʾiššâ: an heiress must marry within her father's tribe so the land stays in it; Q 4:11-12: the shares go to persons (daughters, spouses, parents) with no tribal or land restriction, and a husband inherits from his wife (wa-lakum niṣfu mā taraka azwājukum), which would move property across lines.

passages.text: וְכָל בַּ֞ת יֹרֶ֣שֶׁת נַחֲלָ֗ה מִמַּטּוֹת֮ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ לְאֶחָ֗ד מִמִּשְׁפַּ֛חַת מַטֵּ֥ה אָבִ֖יהָ תִּהְיֶ֣ה לְאִשָּׁ֑ה לְמַ֗עַן יִֽירְשׁוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אִ֖ישׁ נַחֲלַ֥ת אֲבֹתָֽיו

يُوصِيكُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِىٓ أَوْلَٰدِكُمْ لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ ٱلْأُنثَيَيْنِ فَإِن كُنَّ نِسَآءً فَوْقَ ٱثْنَتَيْنِ فَلَهُنَّ ثُلُثَا مَا تَرَكَ وَإِن كَانَتْ وَٰحِدَةً فَلَهَا ٱلنِّصْفُ وَلِأَبَوَيْهِ لِكُلِّ وَٰحِدٍ مِّنْهُمَا ٱلسُّدُسُ مِمَّا تَرَكَ إِن كَانَ لَهُۥ وَلَدٌ فَإِن لَّمْ يَكُن لَّهُۥ وَلَدٌ وَوَرِثَهُۥٓ أَبَوَاهُ فَلِأُمِّهِ ٱلثُّلُثُ فَإِن كَانَ لَهُۥٓ إِخْوَةٌ فَلِأُمِّهِ ٱلسُّدُسُ مِنۢ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ يُوصِى بِهَآ أَوْ دَيْنٍ ءَابَآؤُكُمْ وَأَبْنَآؤُكُمْ لَا تَدْرُونَ أَيُّهُمْ أَقْرَبُ لَكُمْ نَفْعًا فَرِيضَةً مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا

وَلَكُمْ نِصْفُ مَا تَرَكَ أَزْوَٰجُكُمْ إِن لَّمْ يَكُن لَّهُنَّ وَلَدٌ فَإِن كَانَ لَهُنَّ وَلَدٌ فَلَكُمُ ٱلرُّبُعُ مِمَّا تَرَكْنَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ يُوصِينَ بِهَآ أَوْ دَيْنٍ وَلَهُنَّ ٱلرُّبُعُ مِمَّا تَرَكْتُمْ إِن لَّمْ يَكُن لَّكُمْ وَلَدٌ فَإِن كَانَ لَكُمْ وَلَدٌ فَلَهُنَّ ٱلثُّمُنُ مِمَّا تَرَكْتُم مِّنۢ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ تُوصُونَ بِهَآ أَوْ دَيْنٍ وَإِن كَانَ رَجُلٌ يُورَثُ كَلَٰلَةً أَوِ ٱمْرَأَةٌ وَلَهُۥٓ أَخٌ أَوْ أُخْتٌ فَلِكُلِّ وَٰحِدٍ مِّنْهُمَا ٱلسُّدُسُ فَإِن كَانُوٓا۟ أَكْثَرَ مِن ذَٰلِكَ فَهُمْ شُرَكَآءُ فِى ٱلثُّلُثِ مِنۢ بَعْدِ وَصِيَّةٍ يُوصَىٰ بِهَآ أَوْ دَيْنٍ غَيْرَ مُضَآرٍّ وَصِيَّةً مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَلِيمٌ

Only in Sayings on wine, the king's throne and the lamp of YHWH: Bruising wounds scour away evil; blows cleanse the inner chambers; Bread gained by deceit is sweet, but afterwards the mouth is filled with gravel; 'Bad, bad,' says the buyer, then goes away and boasts; Counsel in a man's heart is deep water; a man of understanding draws it out; He who curses father or mother, his lamp is put out in the pupil of darkness; Many proclaim their loyalty, but a faithful man who can find?; The breath (nishmat) of man is the lamp of YHWH, searching all the inner chambers of the belly; A wise king winnows the wicked and drives the threshing wheel over them; It is a snare to say rashly 'Holy!' and only afterwards to reflect on vows; The glory of young men is their strength, the splendor of the old their grey hair; Wine is a mocker and strong drink a brawler; whoever is led astray by it is not wise; A king seated on the throne of judgment winnows all evil with his eyes; and 19 more.

leads.title: Words of the Wise (Amenemope parallel), dining with rulers, winged riches, the orphan's field ↔ One soul, the wombs, orphans' property and the bride-gift
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: Do not enter the fields of the fatherless, for their redeemer (go'el) is strong and will plead their cause (weight 7.3); Guardians must keep orphans' property intact and hand it over when they come of age (weight 6.8). Pair score 14.2.

Only in Words of the Wise (Amenemope parallel), dining with rulers, winged riches, the orphan's field: Do not speak in the ears of a fool, for he will despise the wisdom of your words; Beat the child with the rod and you will save his soul from Sheol; he will not die; Do not eat the bread of the stingy host who says 'eat and drink' while his heart is not with you; you will vomit up the morsel; When dining with a ruler put a knife to your throat and do not crave his delicacies, deceptive food; A section of sayings closely paralleling the Egyptian Instruction of Amenemope; Riches make themselves wings and fly away like an eagle toward heaven; The 'good of eye' (generous) is blessed; the 'evil of eye' (stingy, envious) is to be shunned; He who spares the rod hates his son; corporal discipline of children is commended; Do not move your neighbor's ancient boundary marker.

Only in One soul, the wombs, orphans' property and the bride-gift: Fear God, by whom you ask of one another, and the wombs (kinship ties, al-arḥām); Kin, orphans and the poor present at the division of an estate are given something from it; Property is not handed to the feeble-minded (sufahāʾ); they are fed and clothed from it; Women as well as men receive a fixed share of what parents and kin leave; The husband gives the bride her marriage gift (ṣaduqa, ajr) as her own; she may freely remit part; Those who devour orphans' property devour fire into their bellies; How the first woman was made [divergence between the texts]; A man may marry two, three or four wives, or only one if he fears injustice; A man who seduces an unbetrothed virgin must marry her or pay the bride-price; To whom the bride-price is paid and in what (silver and gold to her father; service to her father; the gift to the woman herself) [divergence between the texts]; Do not covet; each has his own share (in the division among kin); Who receives the marriage payment [divergence between the texts]; and 5 more.

leads.title: Psalm 106, national confession of sins from Egypt to exile ↔ The indictment of Israel; the Messiah not crucified but raised
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/02-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: People make a molten calf while the leader is on the mountain (weight 5.8). Pair score 5.8.

Only in Psalm 106, national confession of sins from Egypt to exile: Israel ate 'sacrifices of the dead' (zivhei metim) at Baal-peor; God caused the exiles to be pitied by all their captors; God grants the people's wilderness craving but sends wasting (razon) into their souls; Provoked at Meribah, Moses spoke rashly with his lips and suffered because of the people; Phinehas's intervention 'was reckoned to him as righteousness for all generations'; Israel 'yokes itself' to Baal of Peor; List of punishment types for the nations: stone-storm, the Shout, swallowing by the earth, drowning; The people exchanged their Glory for the image of an ox that eats grass; Moses 'stood in the breach' (pérets) before God to turn back his wrath from destroying the people; God turned the sea into dry land and they crossed the river on foot; Shed blood pollutes the land and only the killer's blood atones for it; A closing doxology and the divine title it uses [divergence between the texts]; and 16 more.

Only in The indictment of Israel; the Messiah not crucified but raised: Every one of the People of the Book will believe in him before his (or their) death; They did not kill the Messiah Jesus nor crucify him; Israel demands 'show us God openly' and is seized by the thunderbolt; Jesus will be a witness against the People of the Book on resurrection day; It was only made to appear so to them (shubbiha lahum); The Jews' grave slander (buhtān) against Mary; Opponents demand a written book brought down from heaven; God gave the rebellious generation 'statutes that were not good and ordinances by which they could not live', defiling them through offering their firstborn; God raised Jesus up to himself; God raises the mountain (al-Tur) over Israel while taking their covenant [divergence between the texts]; Do not charge interest to the poor of my people [response between the texts]; A request to see God, by the prophet or by the people [divergence between the texts]; and 11 more.

passages.text: وَإِذَا كُنتَ فِيهِمْ فَأَقَمْتَ لَهُمُ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ فَلْتَقُمْ طَآئِفَةٌ مِّنْهُم مَّعَكَ وَلْيَأْخُذُوٓا۟ أَسْلِحَتَهُمْ فَإِذَا سَجَدُوا۟ فَلْيَكُونُوا۟ مِن وَرَآئِكُمْ وَلْتَأْتِ طَآئِفَةٌ أُخْرَىٰ لَمْ يُصَلُّوا۟ فَلْيُصَلُّوا۟ مَعَكَ وَلْيَأْخُذُوا۟ حِذْرَهُمْ وَأَسْلِحَتَهُمْ وَدَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ لَوْ تَغْفُلُونَ عَنْ أَسْلِحَتِكُمْ وَأَمْتِعَتِكُمْ فَيَمِيلُونَ عَلَيْكُم مَّيْلَةً وَٰحِدَةً وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِن كَانَ بِكُمْ أَذًى مِّن مَّطَرٍ أَوْ كُنتُم مَّرْضَىٰٓ أَن تَضَعُوٓا۟ أَسْلِحَتَكُمْ وَخُذُوا۟ حِذْرَكُمْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ أَعَدَّ لِلْكَٰفِرِينَ عَذَابًا مُّهِينًا
وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِم مَّطَرًا فَٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ
وَلَقَدْ أَتَوْا۟ عَلَى ٱلْقَرْيَةِ ٱلَّتِىٓ أُمْطِرَتْ مَطَرَ ٱلسَّوْءِ أَفَلَمْ يَكُونُوا۟ يَرَوْنَهَا بَلْ كَانُوا۟ لَا يَرْجُونَ نُشُورًا
وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِم مَّطَرًا فَسَآءَ مَطَرُ ٱلْمُنذَرِينَ

passages.text: وَٱبْتَلُوا۟ ٱلْيَتَٰمَىٰ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغُوا۟ ٱلنِّكَاحَ فَإِنْ ءَانَسْتُم مِّنْهُمْ رُشْدًا فَٱدْفَعُوٓا۟ إِلَيْهِمْ أَمْوَٰلَهُمْ وَلَا تَأْكُلُوهَآ إِسْرَافًا وَبِدَارًا أَن يَكْبَرُوا۟ وَمَن كَانَ غَنِيًّا فَلْيَسْتَعْفِفْ وَمَن كَانَ فَقِيرًا فَلْيَأْكُلْ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ فَإِذَا دَفَعْتُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ أَمْوَٰلَهُمْ فَأَشْهِدُوا۟ عَلَيْهِمْ وَكَفَىٰ بِٱللَّهِ حَسِيبًا
إِذْ رَءَا نَارًا فَقَالَ لِأَهْلِهِ ٱمْكُثُوٓا۟ إِنِّىٓ ءَانَسْتُ نَارًا لَّعَلِّىٓ ءَاتِيكُم مِّنْهَا بِقَبَسٍ أَوْ أَجِدُ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ هُدًى
إِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِأَهْلِهِۦٓ إِنِّىٓ ءَانَسْتُ نَارًا سَـَٔاتِيكُم مِّنْهَا بِخَبَرٍ أَوْ ءَاتِيكُم بِشِهَابٍ قَبَسٍ لَّعَلَّكُمْ تَصْطَلُونَ

فَلَمَّا قَضَىٰ مُوسَى ٱلْأَجَلَ وَسَارَ بِأَهْلِهِۦٓ ءَانَسَ مِن جَانِبِ ٱلطُّورِ نَارًا قَالَ لِأَهْلِهِ ٱمْكُثُوٓا۟ إِنِّىٓ ءَانَسْتُ نَارًا لَّعَلِّىٓ ءَاتِيكُم مِّنْهَا بِخَبَرٍ أَوْ جَذْوَةٍ مِّنَ ٱلنَّارِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَصْطَلُونَ
